evidence: >>SOURCE FORMAT FREE compiler directive at top
FUNCTION RANDOM() and FUNCTION SECONDS-PAST-MIDNIGHT() intrinsic functions
88-level condition names with SET ... TO TRUE

purpose.summary: A text-based interactive fiction / dungeon-crawl game set in the 'Pyramid of Ahraxis'. The player navigates 28 rooms, collects items (e.g. a shield), manages a character sheet with RPG stats, and tries to exit the pyramid alive with a high score.

notable_features: FUNCTION RANDOM() seeded with FUNCTION SECONDS-PAST-MIDNIGHT() for RNG
OCCURS 28 TIMES for room visit flags with 88-level conditions
Heavy use of GO TO for game-loop control flow (36 GOTOs)
EVALUATE used for command dispatch and room navigation
Character stats rolled with 3d6 simulation using FUNCTION RANDOM()
No EXEC SQL or EXEC CICS
No COPY statements or external CALLs — fully self-contained
verdict.notes: Source is truncated at 16000 chars (room 14 description is cut mid-word 'DISPLA'). The program is a hobby/game-jam project ('INTERACTIVE FICTION GAME JAM', 'THEGRUMPYGAMEDEV') written in GnuCOBOL free format. The heavy reliance on GO TO paragraphs is idiomatic for this style of COBOL game programming. No production indicators (no COMP-3, no file I/O, no CICS/SQL). Classified as student-exercise/demo rather than toy because it is a complete, non-trivial program with real game logic.
